issues.legal_issue: A zonal development plan need not specifically indicate nursery-school land, but a residential colony layout must provide for parks and nursery schools.
material_facts: The dispute arose in an appeal from the dismissal of a writ petition challenging the allotment of land for a nursery school.
The Court considered the statutory requirements for zonal development plans and the rules governing master plans.
The residential layout did not mention a reservation for a park, although the Court found that park space existed at the site.
issues.conclusion: A nursery school need not be specifically shown in a zonal development plan, but the layout for a residential colony must provide for both park space and nursery-school space.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 8(2)(a) and 8(d)(ii) of the Delhi Development Act, 1957, and Rule 4(3)(g) of the Delhi Development (Master Plan and Zonal Development Plan) Rules, 1959, support the requirement that residential-colony layouts provide for parks and nursery schools. A distinction may be made between nursery schools and primary or high schools when deciding what must be indicated in a zonal development plan.

predicates.appeal_challenges_school_land_allotment: Residents appealed after a court dismissed their challenge to an authority's allotment of land for a nursery school.
predicates.residential_colony_layout: The land-use plan at issue was for a residential colony.
predicates.planning_requirements_for_open_space_and: The applicable planning framework addressed open spaces, parks, and educational facilities.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a school-land allotment in a residential-colony layout governed by planning requirements for open space and education, the layout must provide for parks and nursery schools.

issues.legal_issue: A development authority cannot allot land forming part of a park for a nursery school.
material_facts: The Director (Monitoring) reported that part of the park had been enclosed and was being used by the school.
The report stated that the original layout had made no provision for a nursery school in the park and that part of the park was later carved out for that purpose.
The Court found that the land allotted to the school was part of a park.
issues.conclusion: The allotment was a misuse of power, and the allotment was cancelled.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 8(2)(a) and 8(d)(ii) of the Delhi Development Act, 1957, and Rule 4(3)(g) of the Delhi Development (Master Plan and Zonal Development Plan) Rules, 1959, require residential layouts to provide for parks and nursery schools. Land reserved as park space cannot be carved out for a nursery school through an executive or administrative allotment.

predicates.appeal_challenges_land_allotment: Residents appealed against an authority's allotment of land for a school.
predicates.allotted_land_was_part_of_a_park: The land allotted to the school formed part of a park.
predicates.authority_allotted_park_land_for_a_nurse: A development authority allotted park land for use as a nursery school.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an allotment and the authority allotted land forming part of a park for a nursery school, the allotment is cancelled.

issues.legal_issue: An unlawful allotment of park land is not saved by construction on the land or the disruption that relocation may cause to students.
material_facts: The school had constructed a structure on the allotted land, which its counsel described as permanent.
The school argued that removal would cause financial loss and hinder students' educational progress.
The Court cancelled the allotment but allowed the school to continue operating at the site temporarily so that alternative arrangements could be made.
issues.conclusion: The construction and the asserted inconvenience to students did not justify preserving the unlawful allotment, although temporary continuation was allowed to facilitate relocation.
issues.legal_principle: An allotment made in contravention of law is not validated by a structure built on the land or by claims of hardship arising from relocation. The Court may allow temporary continuation to avoid sudden disadvantage to students while alternative arrangements are made.

predicates.appeal_challenges_unlawful_school_land_a: Residents appealed against an allotment used for a school that they said was unlawful.
predicates.allotment_was_contrary_to_law: The land allotment contravened the applicable law.
predicates.school_built_a_structure: The school built a structure on the allotted land.
predicates.relocation_was_claimed_to_disrupt_studen: The school asserted that relocation would disadvantage or disrupt its students.

issues.definition: When a challenged school-land allotment is unlawful and the school has built a structure and claims relocation would disrupt students, the allotment is cancelled while temporary continuation may be allowed.

issues.legal_issue: A development authority must investigate officers responsible for an unauthorized allotment and resulting unauthorized construction.
material_facts: The Court found that the authority had made an unauthorized allotment and that unauthorized construction had been permitted.
The Court observed that officials responsible for illegal allotments or for permitting unauthorized construction should not escape accountability.
The Court directed the authority to investigate and report which officers were responsible.
issues.conclusion: The authority was directed to inquire into the responsible officers and inform the Court.
issues.legal_principle: The Court stated that officers whose illegal actions enable unauthorized construction should be investigated and punished in accordance with law; otherwise, they retain the benefit of their misconduct and encourage similar conduct.

predicates.appeal_reviews_unauthorized_public_land_: An appeal asked the Court to review an authority's allotment of public land alleged to be unauthorized.
predicates.authority_made_an_illegal_allotment: A public authority made an allotment that was found to be illegal.
predicates.unauthorized_construction_was_permitted: Officials permitted construction that was unauthorized.

issues.definition: When an appeal reviews an unauthorized public-land allotment and the authority made an illegal allotment while officials permitted unauthorized construction, the authority must investigate the responsible officers.
